title: The verse explained
hook: Ananda, Mahakaccana and Lomasakangiya each explain the same verse

segments.voice: Yesterday: bhaddekaratta, and your line, see it clearly, right where it is. Did you come back once from the past and once from the future? Today, the same verse, three more times, on a milestone. Day five hundred.
screen: `SEE IT CLEARLY, RIGHT WHERE IT IS.`

segments.voice: Five hundred days. A line heard on day ten can come back differently on day four hundred. Same words, new weight. The next three discourses take yesterday's verse and pass it through four monks. One teaches it from memory. Two first hear of it from a deity, and don't know it. And one explains it when the Buddha leaves it unexplained. It's almost a study in how a teaching travels. Today: the verse explained.
screen: `FIVE HUNDRED DAYS.` → `SAME WORDS, NEW WEIGHT.` → `ONE VERSE, FOUR MONKS.`

segments.voice: In the hundred and thirty-second discourse, Ananda teaches the verse and its explanation to the monks in the assembly hall. The Buddha later asks who taught it, and confirms Ananda got it right. Ananda had heard it and kept it. In the hundred and thirty-third, a monk named Samiddhi goes to bathe at some hot springs near Rajagaha. A deity appears at night and asks: do you know the bhaddekaratta verse? No. Learn it, says the deity. So Samiddhi asks the Buddha, who recites only the verse and goes inside. The monks are left with a short poem and no explanation. They go to Mahakaccana, who was known for unpacking the Buddha's brief sayings. He explains it through the senses: you chase the past when your mind is bound by desire to what the eye once saw, thinking, such was my eye, such were the sights. You build on the future when you set your heart on what the eye will see. The Buddha hears this and says: if you'd asked me, I'd have explained it the same way. In the hundred and thirty-fourth, a monk named Lomasakangiya is asked about the verse by a deity named Candana. He doesn't know the verse. But Candana does, and recites it, saying the Buddha once taught it to the gods. So Lomasakangiya walks all the way to Savatthi to hear it properly. Three discourses, three ways of meeting the same few lines. And the line at the center of the verse, which all of them carry: do today what needs doing, with energy. In Pali, ajja eva kiccam atappam: today itself, the ardent effort.
screen: `ANANDA: HEARD IT AND KEPT IT` · `MAHAKACCANA UNPACKS THE SENSES` · `LOMASAKANGIYA WALKS TO LEARN IT` · `TODAY ITSELF, THE EFFORT` · then, large: `TODAY, THE EFFORT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: recite the verse. Not word for word from any book: a short version in your own words, to keep the way Ananda kept his. Sit and settle. Silently, slowly: don't chase the past. Don't pin hopes on the future. See what's here. Today, the effort. Say it once with each out-breath, then rest in whatever is actually here between the lines. The bell holds the time.
Atappa. Ardor, keen effort: the line that Ananda, Mahakaccana and Lomasakangiya each carried on, as they met the bhaddekaratta verse. Today's word.
Your line: today, the effort. On this five-hundredth day, pick one thing you've been putting off and give it ten honest minutes today. Day five hundred.

howItsDone: Buddhist monastics memorize and chant short verses and study the commentaries that explain them; the bhaddekaratta verse is among those chanted in some communities.

fork.setup: the Buddha recites a short verse and goes into his dwelling without explaining it. you're one of the monks. what do the monks in MN 133 do?
options: go to Mahakaccana and ask him to explain it.
fork.reveal: they go to Mahakaccana, known for expanding the Buddha's brief sayings, and the Buddha approves his explanation.

original.note: Pali atappa: ardor, keen effort. from the verse: today itself, the ardent effort.

trapdoor: what you thought: a verse means one thing, and you learn it once.
what it means: in three discourses, four monks meet the same verse, and each carries it on.

what a scholar hears: MN 132–134 frame the bhaddekaratta verse with different speakers, and MN 133 is one of several suttas where Mahakaccana expands a brief saying (uddesa) into a full exposition (vibhanga).

notes: MN 132–134 paraphrased. Confirm: Samiddhi at the Tapoda hot springs near Rajagaha; Lomasakangiya among the Sakyans, asked by the deity Candana; Candana says the Buddha taught the verse among the Tavatimsa gods.
The Pali 'ajj' eva kiccam atappam' is cited from memory of the verse; confirm spelling (ajjeva kiccam atappam).
Day 500 milestone mentioned lightly in review, hook and carry.

Editor review (days 482–500): the hook miscounted and mischaracterized the monks (it said three, with one who 'knows it but needs it explained'; MN 132–134 involve Ananda, Samiddhi, Mahakaccana and Lomasakangiya, and Samiddhi did not know the verse); fixed hook, screen, match prompt and trapdoor. Removed howItsDone's unsourced retreat custom, which also quoted a modern translation's wording, and the practice's contradiction about Ananda.
